subject: Urgent: Caravel Commerce throughput regression — SDK header reassembly suspected
messages:
From: Sara Nguyen <sara@caravel.com>
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@caravel.com
Date: Tue, 07 Nov 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Spike: Checkout throughput down ~60% this morning

Hi Rafael,

We're seeing a sustained throughput drop on our checkout flow starting ~08:40 PT this morning. Success rate has fallen from 99.6% to ~86% and p95 latency jumped from ~280ms to >1.2s. We rolled back our app twice, but the issue persists.

Attached are a set of client-side captures and a short tokenized request sample. The traces show many requests stalling at the initial L7 response — we see a large backlog of tokens in the client logs.

This is impacting checkout conversions across multiple regions. Can Redwood advise ASAP? We're on a tight sales event this weekend and need an ETA for mitigation.

Attachments: capture-logs-20281107.zip, client-pcap-sample-11-07.txt

Thanks,
Sara Nguyen
Sr. Platform Engineer, Caravel Commerce
From: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
To: Sara Nguyen <sara@caravel.com>, ops@caravel.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 07 Nov 2028 09:35:00 -08:00

- Approx concurrent requests during the spike? (ballpark fine)

Ben (infra) + Marissa (SDK) — looping you in to prioritize. I'll coordinate with Caravel through the thread.

Rafael

On Tue, Nov 7, 2028 at 09:35 AM Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Ben (infra) + Marissa (SDK) — looping you in to prioritize.

Thanks Rafael. Initial look at ingress metrics shows a large increase in parse failures and transient 5xx errors from one of our edge clusters in us-west-2 starting 08:38. Error payloads align with a downstream codec exception in our streaming parser: "incomplete header frame".

Marissa — SDK team: Caravel is on v2.3.1 of the client. Their captures show frequent small TCP writes that look like header frames being sent split across packets (likely due to client-side connection pooling under high concurrency). Our streaming parser has a header reassembly path that is susceptible to out-of-order or highly fragmented header sequences under a specific flush pattern — we're seeing a code path that returns an intermediate parse error rather than waiting to reassemble. That triggers an internal retry loop and amplifies load, making the issue manifest as throughput drop.

Immediate mitigation options:
- Apply a temporary routing rule to route Caravel to a different parser config (more permissive reassembly buffer) — low risk and can be rolled in <30m.
- Patch the parser to be tolerant (needs code change + canary, ETA 36–48h).

Rafael — I'll coordinate the routing rule with infra. Marissa, can you validate the reassembly tolerance patch?

Ben Carter
Sr. SRE, Redwood Inference
From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: ben.carter@redwood.ai, rafael.mendes@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: Sara Nguyen <sara@caravel.com>, ops@caravel.com
Date: Tue, 07 Nov 2028 11:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Spike: Checkout throughput down ~60% this morning

Agree with Ben's assessment. Repro notes from SDK instrumentation: when clients send header blocks split into three or more sub-writes within <5ms windows, our current reassembly code can hit a fast-fail path that surfaces as a parse exception. This is rare in normal traffic but Caravel's bursty checkout concurrency combined with their connection pooling exposes it.

Planned actions:
1) Apply a route-level parser override for Caravel to use the permissive reassembly policy. This should drop their error rate immediately. (I can deploy the override now; it requires an infra rollout.)
2) Create a targeted SDK patch (v2.3.2) to harden header reassembly and add a unit test for fragmented header sequences — target canary tomorrow 11/08 and full rollout 11/09 if canary looks good.
3) Add telemetry to detect fragmentation patterns and automatically increase reassembly timeout for affected customers.

Temporary rollback plan: if the route override causes regressions we'll revert in 15 minutes; I'll monitor active error-rate dashboards.

Marissa Cole
Lead SDK Engineer, Redwood Inference

Rafael

We appreciate the canary plan. We also want to flag that this was high-impact for our Black Friday prep — we'll follow up with CS on the credit request. Please include the patch details and a short summary we can attach to our incident report.

Sara
Sr. Platform Engineer, Caravel Commerce
